text:
Elena: Need a compact one-sheet for webinar follow-up — audience = platform security + procurement. Must compare Hosted / Dedicated / Private, include two safe benchmark callouts (no raw numbers), and send inbound to a gated routing form. Keep it scannable and buyer-focused.
Kai: I can draft. Leaning 3 stacked cards + a 3-row micro-compare and a tiny SDR triage checklist. Use safe phrasing: 'low p95 latency profiles' and 'meaningful unit-cost improvements with batching/quantization'. Link to benchmark hub ID BK-2024-11 rather than numbers.
Ben: Add a short buyer-signal section for SDRs: Data residency? SLA required? Throughput band? That helps routing to the right lane. Keep it 3 bullets.
Elena: Also: avoid naming KMS vendors; don't claim turnkey air-gapped installs. Safe line: 'Configurable networking, KMS integrations, and audit logging.' Add legal footnote: 'Performance varies by model, hardware, and prompt patterns.'
Legal-Bot: Reminder: any benchmark citation must reference BK-2024-11 and include Ops sign-off. Tagging @Ops.
Kai: Draft copy below — quick read and then I'll make the PDF. Reply with edits.

```
Secure inference: pick the deployment that matches your controls

Hosted — Fastest time-to-value
- Why: API-first hosted inference for rapid experiments and feature rollouts.
- Security: Shared infra with tenant isolation and RBAC.
- Typical buyer: product teams validating features.

Dedicated — Predictable capacity & SLAs
- Why: Reserved GPU pools and configurable autoscaling for steady production throughput.
- Security: Data-isolated pools and stronger access controls.
- Typical buyer: teams needing SLA-backed performance.

Private — Compliance-first control
- Why: VPC and on-prem deployment options with audit logs and customer KMS integrations.
- Security: Network isolation and enterprise policy enforcement.
- Typical buyer: regulated and security-sensitive organizations.

At-a-glance (Security | SLA | Typical buyer)
- Hosted: Shared controls | Best-effort latency | Prototyping
- Dedicated: Isolated pools | SLA-backed | Production scale
- Private: Full control | Configurable SLAs | Regulated workloads

Benchmarks: See BK-2024-11 for latency profiles by model/region and cost comparison notes. Performance varies by model, hardware, and prompt patterns.

SDR triage (3 quick signals):
- Data residency: Yes / No
- SLA required: Yes / No
- Peak throughput: low | medium | high

Routing CTA: Book a deployment review (shortlink: redwood.ai/route) — captures buyer signals and routes to the correct sales lane.

Legal footnote: Performance and unit costs vary by model, hardware, and workload. Contact Sales for private deployment packaging; options vary by customer.
```

Ben: Looks tight. One edit: change throughput bands to explicit tags we use in CRM: low (<2k), mid (2k-20k), high (>20k).
Elena: Good catch, update and add @Ops to reviewers for final sign-off. Owner: Kai. Reviewers: @Ben, @Elena, @Ops. Timeline: PDF draft tomorrow AM, final by Friday EOD.
Ops: Acknowledged — will review BK-2024-11 link before publish.
